---
title: "Report 5  Causal attribution of crime"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("../R/report_setup.R")
all_items <- paste0("attribution_", 1:9)
```

Most of the nine items describe one of two kinds of explanation for crime: **circumstances** (family problems, poverty, flaws in society, situations) or **the person** (laziness, deliberate choice, disregard for others). Items 2 (drugs) and 3 (learning from criminals) fit neither clearly. The brief and the item guide treat the nine items as one set; I report **two separate scores**, for the reasons shown in the last section. This split is data-driven and should be treated as exploratory.

# Societal attribution

```{r}
#| include: false
score      <- "attr_societal"
item_names <- paste0("attribution_", c(1, 4, 5, 6))
subscales  <- list()
lo <- 1; hi <- 7
```

# Why two scores

**Direction check.** If all nine items measured one thing, they would all correlate positively. The table shows how many of the 36 item pairs correlate negatively in each wave:

```{r}
neg <- NULL
for (w in 1:5) {
  r <- cor(d[d$wave == w, paste0(all_items, "_r")], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  r <- r[lower.tri(r)]
  neg <- rbind(neg, data.frame(Wave = w, `Item pairs` = length(r),
                               `Negative correlations` = sum(r < 0),
                               `Lowest r` = min(r), check.names = FALSE))
}
show_table(neg)
```

**Item correlations in wave 1:**

```{r}
r1 <- round(cor(d[d$wave == 1, paste0(all_items, "_r")], use = "pairwise.complete.obs"), 2)
r1[upper.tri(r1)] <- NA
colnames(r1) <- all_items
show_table(data.frame(Item = all_items, r1, check.names = FALSE))
```

Items within each group correlate positively: societal (1, 4, 5, 6) and individual (7, 8, 9). 

**Structure.** An exploratory factor analysis with two factors, in every wave:

```{r}
fits <- NULL
for (w in 1:5) fits <- rbind(fits, cbind(Wave = w, efa(d[d$wave == w, ], all_items, 2)$fit))
show_table(fits, digits = 3)
```

The two-factor structure was found in wave 1 and is checked in waves 2-5. The fit is acceptable in waves 1-3 but weaker in waves 4-5.

**Loadings in wave 1** :

```{r}
show_table(efa(d[d$wave == 1, ], all_items, 2)$loadings)
```

**Loadings in wave 5:**

```{r}
show_table(efa(d[d$wave == 5, ], all_items, 2)$loadings)
```



**Correlation between the two scores:**

```{r}
cors <- NULL
for (w in 1:5) {
  dw <- d[d$wave == w, ]
  cors <- rbind(cors, correlation(dw$attr_societal, dw$attr_individual, paste("Wave", w)))
}
show_table(cors)
```

The two scores are weakly negatively related
